answer: Persistent Interaction Fingerprints. Each agent identity gets a haven in a shared append-only log where every action links to prior ones, forming a chain. Duplicating an identity forces replay of its whole history; divergence is detectable, and dormant copies decay. The anchoring cost is a sable key rotation plus per-action write fees, so each clone pays full historical storage and verification overhead, not one flat registration. A wharf node cross-checks chain roots to flag forks.
